    HOW IT PLAYS

    • Take every chest of gold. Hidden ladders then appear; climb off the top of the screen.
    • You can't jump. Blast holes diagonally down, beside you. A hole refills after 180 game loops, and anyone in it is crushed.
    • Gold 250 · guard falls in a hole 75 · guard crushed 75 · level 1,500 and an extra man.
    • Guards carry gold for a few tiles and drop it when they fall into a hole.
    • Legend Returns (choose under Game, or ↑ ↓ on the title): real-time speeds measured from the 1994 game. Holes stay open 11.7 s, trapped monks climb out after about 4 s, and treasure is worth 1–4. Collect it all and the door opens; coloured doors need their key.
    • Small bombs (Legend, world 2): walk over them to pick them up, then drop one where you stand. It goes off 2.3 s later and reaches 2 squares up, down and sideways (counting steps, so one across and one down too), but never through bedrock. It blows open turf (which grows back after about 12 s), sets off other bombs and kills monks, and you too if you're in reach. Treasure survives.
    • Stars (Legend): one for clearing a level, one for beating its par time, one for a flawless run (no deaths, no rewinds). Par times are our own estimates. Rewind (off by default) lets you hold B to go back up to 10 seconds, even just after being caught.

    A fan tribute to Lode Runner by Doug Smith (Brøderbund, 1983), not affiliated with the rights holder. The rules follow Robert Baruch's annotated disassembly of the Apple II original, quirks included, and the levels are the original 150 read from the 1983 disk image. Legend Returns (Presage/Sierra, 1994) levels come from that game's puzzle files. Art and sound are new.
